about: Reference-table verification for the periodic-trend pickers (src/lib/teaching/sceneGenerators/periodicTrends.pure.ts): the 17 elements' Pauling electronegativity and the radius series compared with authoritative tables, and every ordered pair whose order depends on the scale chosen.
enSource: Pauling EN of all 17 elements equals the 'WEL' column (WebElements; Allred 1961 / Huheey 1993) of Wikipedia 'Electronegativities of the elements (data page)' and the Pauling table in Wikipedia 'Electronegativity' (both identical, 17/17 exact). The data page also has CRC (84th ed.) and Lange sub-columns, but the flattened extraction could not assign them reliably, so agreement with the CRC Handbook column itself is UNVERIFIED (not fetched separately); WebElements page https://www.webelements.com/periodicity/electronegativity_pauling/ returned 404.
radiusScaleOfRepoNumbers: 'Calculated atomic radius' (Clementi, Raimondi & Reinhardt 1963/1967 SCF screening constants): 17/17 repo values equal the 'Calculated' column of Wikipedia 'Atomic radii of the elements (data page)'. They are NOT the empirical (Slater 1964) radii (0/17 equal: e.g. Na 180, Cl 100) and NOT covalent radii (Cordero 2008: Na 166, Cl 102). The calculated H = 53 pm is flagged 'citation needed' on Wikipedia.

perElement.notes: Wikipedia flags the calculated H = 53 pm as 'citation needed' (equals the Bohr radius 52.9 pm).

summary.note: Each unordered pair here corresponds to two ordered pairs (A,B) and (B,A) that both flip. Ties count as differing. Radius comparison scales: Slater empirical, Cordero 2008 covalent (C = sp3 76), and the covalent column printed on the Wikipedia data page (WebElements-sourced, older: e.g. C 75, F 64). EN comparison is repo (Pauling) vs Allen 1989/2000 as an alternative scale; Pauling-vs-CRC/Lange columns were not separable.
